idiom_name: Bunny connection/channel with Queue#subscribe blocks and Exchange#publish
implementation_notes: Ruby's block syntax replaces the listener/factory structure: `queue.subscribe do |delivery_info, properties, payload| ... end` registers the inbound adapter callback on Bunny's worker pool, and `exchange.publish(payload, routing_key: ...)` is the outbound half, so a small class or module holding the connection and channel is the whole adapter. Bunny provides the connection, channel, exchange and queue primitives (plus manual_ack, prefetch and durable queues), and the adapter's job is to convert application objects to payloads and route incoming payloads to application methods (method(:call) or a block). Keep Bunny objects out of the application-facing signatures; use a separate channel per consumer thread.
pitfalls: Queue#subscribe runs the block on Bunny's internal worker pool: an exception escaping it can tear down the connection, so the adapter must rescue and reject/ack explicitly.

Without manual_ack the message is acknowledged on delivery; with manual_ack the adapter must call delivery_info.ack only after the handler succeeded, or the broker redelivers and the application sees duplicates.
A channel is not meant to be shared for consuming across threads: use one channel per consumer thread and keep publishing on its own channel.
